meta.title: How a Run reaches the screen
meta.description: One autopilot turn, from prompt to the two places a plan is displayed. Shows why the RFX planner sees the plan and the in-chat strip does not: they read different endpoints, built from the same event log by different code, with different failure behaviour.

nodes.label: Agent Loop
nodes.sublabel: observe → think → act, one iteration at a time

nodes.label: Plan gate
nodes.sublabel: first call is restricted to commit_plan
nodes.note: Asks the model to divide the task. If the model answers with TEXT instead of a tool call, the prose is translated into a real plan and committed anyway ("plan written as text — translated and committed"). That salvage is why the planner has a plan at all: the model has not once called commit_plan as a tool in the runs on record.

nodes.label: Episodic writer
nodes.sublabel: appends every event as it happens

nodes.label: events.jsonl
nodes.sublabel: the ONLY source of truth · plan, tool.call, tool.result, checkpoint, turn.close, error
nodes.note: ~/.crv/sessions/<id>/events.jsonl. Both display paths are derived from this one file. Nothing else is persisted, so anything the UI shows is a projection built on read.

nodes.label: GET /state
nodes.note: Hands back the plan exactly as committed — titles, details, files. It makes no claim about what is finished; there is no status field to be wrong about.

nodes.label: GET /report
nodes.sublabel: INTERPRETED · plan + a status per step
nodes.note: 404s with "no plan in this session" until a plan event exists. That 404 is the first half of the chat bug: the panel's fetch helper turns any non-200 into null.

flags.title: Two endpoints for one plan, and only the simpler one is reliable
flags.note: /state and /report are both built from the same events.jsonl on every request. /state hands back the plan verbatim and cannot be wrong about progress because it makes no claim. /report adds a status per step, and every bug in this diagram lives in that added interpretation: the 404 before a plan exists, the disk inference, the false "done". The planner survives on the plain endpoint and derives progress itself from the files it can see.
flags.fix: Make the strip read what the planner reads: take the plan from /state so it appears the moment it commits and cannot be erased by a 404, and treat per-step status as an overlay that arrives later when /report has something real to say. The strip then shows the steps during the run even before any status is known — which is the whole point of a progress indicator.

nodes.label: BuildReportAt
nodes.sublabel: decides done / partial / pending per step
nodes.note:
Status comes from checkpoint events. When there are none it falls back to DISK RECONCILIATION: if every file a step declared exists, call it done.

Zero checkpoints have been written in any run on record, so this fallback decides every status. It was also reporting 4/4 done for a plan whose four steps all declared index.html — fixed 2026-09-04 to require a step's files to be its own.

flags.title: Step status is inferred from disk because no checkpoint is ever written
flags.note: BuildReportAt prefers checkpoint events and falls back to disk reconciliation. Every run on record has ZERO checkpoint events, so the fallback is not a fallback — it is the only source of truth for "done". Existence of a file cannot distinguish which step wrote it, and can never show that a verification passed. That is how the car run reported 4/4 green, Verify included, while the turn was dying in a check_page loop. The shared-files case is fixed, but the underlying gap remains: the loop never records that a step finished, so a plan whose steps DO own distinct files is still marked done the moment the file appears, not when the step's work succeeded.
flags.fix: Have the loop write a checkpoint event when it moves off a step: which step, whether its tool calls succeeded, and what verified it. Then disk reconciliation goes back to being a fallback for chat-mode turns, and "done" means the work was observed, not that a file exists.

nodes.label: RFX bridge
nodes.note: Fetches /state and /events on its own timer, independently of the chat store.

nodes.label: Planner panel
nodes.sublabel: a CONTROL surface · shows the tree, runs steps
nodes.note: ~/.crv/rfx/planner/ui/panel.html. Renders whatever rfx.session().plan holds, and checks the declared files itself via rfx.files(). It is not told which steps are done — it derives that, which is why it survived the false-done bug in the report.

nodes.label: Session store
nodes.note: loadReport() assigns the fetch result UNCONDITIONALLY, and the fetch helper returns null for any non-200. So every poll during the seconds before the plan commits overwrites `report` with null — and the poll was gated on `report` being set in the first place.

flags.title: A failed poll erases the plan the strip is waiting for
flags.note: loadReport() does `report = await api.report(id)` with no guard, and the fetch helper returns null for ANY non-200. /report answers 404 with "no plan in this session" for the first seconds of every turn, before the plan event exists — three seconds in the car run. So each poll in that window assigns null. Combined with the poll being gated on `report` already being set, the strip could never appear: the only unconditional fetches happen after the turn ends, by which time the plan reads complete and the strip archives itself on arrival. The planner is immune because it reads /state, which returns the plan verbatim and is never gated.
flags.fix: Keep the last good report: only assign when the fetch returns a value, and clear it explicitly on session switch (where it is already reset). Poll whenever a turn is running, not only once a report exists.

nodes.label: Plan strip
nodes.sublabel: a PROGRESS surface · above the composer
nodes.note: Renders only when store.report is non-null. Archives itself once every step reads done, and remembers that in localStorage per plan id — so a plan that arrives ALREADY complete is hidden the instant it appears.

nodes.label: Brain Core
nodes.sublabel: Qwen3.8-27B · the thing being asked for a plan

nodes.sublabel: the files the build actually produces
